original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: Exact minimum of five paid coordinate-CNOT calls for diag([a],[b],[aba]) in M_3(F2[GL_2(F2)]), with only a and b paid labels, arbitrary dirty register data, and free scalar GL3(F2) mixing.
scope_change_reason: The open-ended register-model card is narrowed to one heterogeneous three-target word in the existing two-generator nonabelian alphabet. This differs from the repeated-SWAP targets in PR1414/1491 and from the two-register GL3 address family in open PR1567.
bottleneck_link: A shorter word would remove one paid rank-one call from this finite bit-register mechanism. The exact five-call minimum rules out that local saving; no supplier-wide embedding or kappa change is claimed.
stop_rule: Enumerate the complete formal radius-two ball and decide all words of length at most four by the radius-two meet-in-the-middle split. Stop after that exact decision and the five-call direct control.
evidence: EXPECTED.json binds the 1,807-state radius-two ball, its 56 generators and 28 projectors, zero inverse-target intersections through length four, and a formal five-call witness. verify.py independently encodes the full six-element group algebra and checks dirty-boundary and mutation controls.
author: Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance with the mathematical search, standalone verifier, proof explanation and package. No independent human proof review is claimed.

open_questions.question: What is the exact minimum for the same heterogeneous target when one or more restored dirty registers are added?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The present equality is fixed to exactly three registers and does not rule out a fourth register enabling cross-target sharing.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the exact state encoding to r=4 and first apply augmentation/sign constraints to reduce the length range before enumerating.
open_questions.blocked_by: The rank-one idempotent and formal-state inventories grow quickly; the active four-SWAP claim is a different target and must remain separately coordinated.
